studies.comparison_type: High quartile versus low quartile of Western diet

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: In order to explore the role of broader eating patterns in the etiology of prostate cancer, we conducted a principal components analysis among Uruguayan men. extraction_supporting_text.comparison: high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet
extraction_supporting_text.design: The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.35 (95% CI: 1.0–1.82), suggesting that western pattern diet is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 57.15%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
